Look up references in a database's sources by key

Source: R/sources.R
traits_build_sources.Rd

The sources component of a traits.build database holds the bibliographic references for every dataset, as a RefManageR::BibEntry() object keyed by citation key (for example "Falster_2005"). austraits gives it the extra class traits_build_sources, which makes $ look an entry up by its key. Any of these return the reference for Falster_2005:

database$sources$Falster_2005
database$sources[["Falster_2005"]]
database$sources["Falster_2005"]

and database$sources[c("Falster_2003", "Falster_2005")] returns several. Use names(database$sources) to list the keys.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'traits_build_sources'
x$name

# S3 method for class 'traits_build_sources'
x[i, j, ..., drop = FALSE]

# S3 method for class 'traits_build_sources'
c(..., recursive = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A traits_build_sources object: the sources component of a traits.build database.

name

A citation key, or a BibEntry field name.

i, j, ..., drop

Indices, as for RefManageR's [ method for BibEntry.

recursive

Ignored, as for RefManageR's c() method for BibEntry.

Value

For $, the entry with key name as a traits_build_sources object of length one or, when name is not a key, the value of field name for every entry. For [ and c(), a traits_build_sources object.

Details

On a plain BibEntry, $ is field access (sources$title returns the title of every entry), so sources$Falster_2005 returns a list of NULLs, one per entry, instead of the reference. With the traits_build_sources class, $ looks up by key when the name is a key, and otherwise falls back to field access, so sources$title and sources$author work as before.

The class only adds behaviour; everything else is inherited from BibEntry. Printing, format(), RefManageR::WriteBib() and RefManageR::toBiblatex() give the same output with or without it. [, [[ and c() keep the class (for c(), when the first argument has it), as do the RefManageR methods built on [, such as sort(), unique() and head(). RefManageR's replacement functions ($<-, [<-, [[<-) and merge() return a plain BibEntry.

bind_databases(), load_austraits() and extract_data() (and so the other extract_*() functions) add the class to the sources they return, including for databases built before the class existed. An object carrying the class behaves as a plain BibEntry in a session where austraits is not loaded.

See also

bind_databases(), load_austraits(), RefManageR::BibEntry()

Examples

sources <- c(
  RefManageR::BibEntry(
    bibtype = "Article", key = "Falster_2003",
    title = "Leaf size and angle vary widely across species",
    author = "Daniel S. Falster and Mark Westoby",
    journal = "New Phytologist", year = 2003
  ),
  RefManageR::BibEntry(
    bibtype = "Article", key = "Falster_2005",
    title = "Alternative height strategies among 45 dicot rain forest species",
    author = "Daniel S. Falster and Mark Westoby",
    journal = "Journal of Ecology", year = 2005
  )
)
database <- list(sources = sources)

# Without the class, `$` with a key returns a list of NULLs
database$sources$Falster_2005
#> $Falster_2003
#> NULL
#> 
#> $Falster_2005
#> NULL
#> 

# bind_databases(), load_austraits() and extract_data() add the class
class(database$sources) <- c("traits_build_sources", class(database$sources))
database$sources$Falster_2005
#> [1] D. S. Falster and M. Westoby. “Alternative height strategies among
#> 45 dicot rain forest species”. In: _Journal of Ecology_ (2005).
database$sources[["Falster_2005"]]
#> [1] D. S. Falster and M. Westoby. “Alternative height strategies among
#> 45 dicot rain forest species”. In: _Journal of Ecology_ (2005).

# Names that are not keys are still field access
database$sources$year
#> $Falster_2003
#> [1] "2003"
#> 
#> $Falster_2005
#> [1] "2005"
#>
